text: WAVE 0 � TRACK � THIS SURFACE HAD NO WRITE LAW. POST /api/comment had no x-uni-cc, no Origin check, no peer check and no content-type check, on a server bound to 0.0.0.0. text:
lab-l5: a REPRODUCIBLE failure at last -- the gate convicted itself for tidying, and git needs -f -f

FIRST CAPTURED FAILURE OF THE FLAKY GATE. Four runner passes on 2026-07-29 gave PASS, FAIL, PASS,
FAIL; a read-only harness gave PASS, PASS, PASS; and gate_runner.cjs:82 buffers each gate's stdout so
NO FAILING RUN'S OUTPUT HAD EVER BEEN SEEN. It is now reproducible on demand, in one command, and it
prints a distinctive line:

  FAIL  the runs did not touch the working tree, and left no worktree behind
        - -1 worktree(s) leaked by this gate's own runs
  GATE: FAIL - lab-l5, 25/26 checks    exit=1

A NEGATIVE LEAK. The gate failed itself for REMOVING a worktree.

TWO DEFECTS, BOTH MEASURED.

(1) ONE --force CANNOT REMOVE A LOCKED WORKTREE. `git worktree add` holds a lock named
"initializing" for the duration of the add and releases it on completion; an interrupted add leaves
it locked FOREVER. desk.cjs's finish() used `git worktree remove --force`. Against a real stray left
in this repository by the very runner pass in which lab-l5 failed -- uni-desk-26YkxK, at 8e40bf6, two
commits stale -- git answered:

  $ git worktree remove --force .../uni-desk-26YkxK
  fatal: cannot remove a locked working tree, lock reason: initializing
  use 'remove -f -f' to override or unlock first                        exit 128
  $ git worktree remove -f -f .../uni-desk-26YkxK                       exit 0, silent

And `worktree prune` cannot clean up after it either -- prune SKIPS locked worktrees. Proved by the
control sitting beside it: a sibling stray that was merely `prunable` was pruned away in the same
period while the locked one survived every prune. Fixed: `-f -f`, with git's own transcript in the
comment so nobody "simplifies" it back.

(2) THE GATE COMPARED COUNTS, SO IT COULD NOT TELL A LEAK FROM A TIDY-UP. verify_lab_l5.cjs computed
`leaked = worktreesAfter - worktreesBefore` and required `leaked === 0`, so BOTH directions failed,
and BOTH printed "N worktree(s) leaked by this gate's own runs". But desk.cjs's finish() calls
`git worktree prune` UNCONDITIONALLY, which deletes strays this gate never created -- so the gate's
own cleanup moved the delta and then convicted the gate for it. The old comment said the delta was
used precisely so "a stray left by something else is a different fact that must not be laundered into
L5's verdict"; THE DELTA COULD NOT ACHIEVE THAT, because L5's own run removes those strays. Fixed to
a SET DIFFERENCE in both directions: `appeared` (present after, absent before) is a real leak and the
only thing that may fail this check; `vanished` is tidying and is now reported out loud, not punished.

MUTATION-PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, ON THE SAME FIXTURE -- a planted prunable stray (worktree added,
its directory deleted, the registration left):
  OLD code, from `git show HEAD:` and run unmodified: FAIL, 25/26, "-1 worktree(s) leaked", exit 1.
  NEW code, same fixture:                            PASS, 26/26, and it SAYS what happened --
     "NO worktree path present afterwards is one this gate added (1 pre-existing besides the main
      tree). It also REMOVED 1 pre-existing stray(s) it did not create."
  NEW code, clean tree: PASS 26/26 in 33s, zero worktrees left behind.
The old version was run for real rather than reasoned about, because deriving the old behaviour from
quoted source is exactly the shortcut that has produced four wrong claims in this session.

WHY IT ONLY BIT INSIDE THE RUNNER, AND WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED. Standalone on a clean
repository there are no strays, the delta is 0, and it passes -- which is why three harness runs and
every standalone run passed. Inside the runner, worktree litter is present: lab-l6's gauntlet drives
the same desk, resonance L1 adds its own worktree, and lab_server.cjs:329 runs the gauntlet ON BOOT
while :54 and :85 guard one-run-at-a-time PER PROCESS ONLY -- the gate runner is a different process,
so nothing serialises `git worktree add/remove/prune` between them. THAT CROSS-PROCESS RACE IS NOT
PROVED. What is proved is a mechanism that makes this gate fail intermittently, a reproduction of it,
and a fix for both halves. The specific trigger of the 07-29 failures was never captured and this
commit does not claim to have found it -- but the failure now prints a distinctive line, so a
recurrence will be identifiable instead of anonymous.

ALSO CLEANED: the locked stray uni-desk-26YkxK, which had been sitting in this repository since the
failing run, was removed with `-f -f`. `git worktree list` is back to one entry.

MEASURED: lab-l5 26/26 PASS in 33s clean · 26/26 PASS with a foreign stray, reporting the tidy-up ·
old version 25/26 FAIL on the same fixture · node --check clean on both files.

resonance: --prove went from 721 SECONDS to 0.12, so the meter finally runs in CI

THE INSTRUMENT NOBODY COULD AFFORD TO RUN. resonance_meter.cjs --prove is invoked by no CI job, no
script and no registry entry, and its own header explains why it is deliberately not a gate: as a
registered verify_* file it RECURSED, because layer L2 measures whether the instruments run BY
RUNNING gate_runner, and the runner runs every registered gate. That reasoning is correct and is
untouched here. But the reason nobody ran it by hand was simpler: MEASURED 2026-07-30, `--prove` took
721 SECONDS. Twelve minutes. It is now 0.12s, the same 10/10 checks.

The cause: prove() opened with `if (!real) real = R.measure();` and the --prove entry point calls
prove() with NO ARGUMENT. So the flag whose entire purpose is the STUBBED, instant lattice arithmetic
first ran a full real measurement -- four gate_runner invocations, a git worktree add/remove at L1,
and `mix test` at L6 -- and `real` feeds EXACTLY ONE THING: the headline narrator line, which the
comment beside it already declares is not a counted check. Twelve minutes of gate runs to print one
sentence that proves nothing about the meter, in the one file whose header says "the whole thing is
instant".

MADE OPTIONAL, NOT DELETED: the main path still measures for real and passes the result in, so the
full reading is unchanged there. Only --prove skips it, and it SAYS "NOT MEASURED on this run.
UNMEASURED IS NOT A PASS." rather than printing a hopeful blank.

AND THE ONE-LINE VERSION OF THIS FIX CRASHES -- caught by an adversarial verifier before it shipped,
not after. Deleting the assignment alone is not enough: the headline dereferences `real.resonant`
SIX LINES ABOVE the line that looks like the culprit, so on the --prove path it would throw a
TypeError and turn the proof into a stack trace. Every read of `real` is now guarded.

NOW IN CI, by name rather than by registry, in the gates-node job. That is the first time this
instrument has been run by anything other than a human typing it.

L3: THE TWO UNRULED GATES ARE RULED. MUTATION_EVIDENCE carried 28 entries against a 30-gate registry
-- `claims` and `sight-blind`, both registered earlier today, arrived unruled. That is the layer
working as designed ("A new gate must be ruled on, not counted by default"), and it is why L3 was the
first unsatisfied layer. Both carry real, targeted, negative-controlled mutations, so both get a
string anchor rather than null: claims -> "MUTATION: every check bites" (verify_claims.cjs:411),
sight-blind -> "NEGATIVE CONTROL: the unmutated page passes". Both verified to survive codeOnly(),
which strips whole-line comments -- an anchor surviving only in a comment would let a gutted gate
still count as proven. Now 30/30 ruled, 0 unruled, 0 anchors rotted.

L3 STAYS PARTIAL, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT READING. Six gates remain DECLARED to have no mutation
proof at all (gaia-lint, schema-pointers, overlays, colony, lab-l0, lab-l1). The unruled count
reaching zero is not the layer clearing, and it must not be reported as such.

MY OWN GATE'S MUTATIONS WERE UNREACHABLE UNDER THE RUNNER, AND THAT IS FIXED TOO. verify_sight_blind
ran its four mutations only under --prove, and gate_runner spawns every gate with no argv beyond the
file path -- so in the only place the gate is ever executed automatically, THE MUTATIONS NEVER FIRED.
A green sight-blind in a CI sweep would have been evidence the checks pass and NO evidence they can
still fail: the exact "unlicensed green" resonance L7 exists to name, shipped inside the gate written
to stop a HUD claiming health it had not measured. There was precedent for the flag-gated shape
(lab-l2-shot is declared with the anchor "--mutate" and is likewise out of band), so it was
defensible rather than wrong -- it is still worse. The mutations are pure in-memory string edits
costing ~2 ms TOTAL; there was never a budget argument. Now in-band: 9/9 checks + 5/5 mutations in
24 ms with no flag.

A FALSE COMMENT DELETED: resonance_meter.cjs said check 3b was supplied by
`checkARealProbeDetectsARealBreak()`. No such function has ever existed -- check 3b is an anonymous
inline block. Found by a verifier that was auditing something else.

23 PASS / 4 FAIL this morning, with lab-l5 and lab-l6 BOTH GREEN (the worktree fix at bab368e) ·
resonance_meter --prove 10/10 in 0.12s, was 721s · sight-blind 9/9 + 5/5 in 24ms · L3 30/30 ruled ·
node --check clean on all four files · ci.yml parses, gates-node now has five steps. The two

METHOD NOTE. The five defects this commit acts on were measured by five independent read-only
